A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L-WISE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original human categorization and learning experiments, including moth, dermoscopy, and histology tasks, alongside model comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses of perturbation locations, trial inclusion, and model training checkpoints.

M1.justification: L-WISE retains robustified guide models, ground-truth-logit enhancement, difficulty-percentile selection, and the same curriculum schedules. The reorganized explanation and additional experimental settings do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet animal categorization, iNaturalist moth images, HAM10000 dermoscopy, and MHIST histology. The added analyses reuse existing data and task coverage; no new domain, population, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained: c-score, prediction depth, adversarial robustness, the six guide-model configurations, CLAHE/MSRCR/Lightroom controls, cross-entropy enhancement, and ET/DS ablations. The new checkpoint analysis varies training progress within an existing model.

E3.justification: v2 broadens the reported ImageNet regression pool to include vanilla/CutMix perturbation trials and adds an original-image-only comparison. Its checkpoint study introduces a separate 90-epoch training schedule. Appendix S1 also revises the blanket ceil(2epsilon) enhancement-step setting to ceil(4epsilon) for XCiT, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary validation: Fig. S2 analyzes spatial perturbation concentration, Fig. S5 tests sensitivity to trial inclusion, and Fig. S8 examines difficulty prediction and example enhancements across training checkpoints. These address additional questions about perturbation behavior and dependence on analysis choices and model maturity; existing ablations remain.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies Wald tests for logistic-regression coefficients and stratified 500-fold cross-validation for appendix AUC estimates. The existing 95% bootstrap intervals, 10,000 bootstrap replicates, and participant power analysis remain. No increase in independent runs is established.

E6.justification: Fig. 1 reports AUC 0.72 instead of 0.71 alongside broader trial pooling; new Fig. S5 reports 0.719 pooled versus 0.711 for unmodified images. Appendix AUC plots are revised, and spatial/checkpoint results are added. The moth enhancement association changes from nonsignificant p=0.14 to p<0.05 (v1 Fig. S11; v2 Fig. S14), without explanation. Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The difficulty ranking, enhancement objective and update, dropout calculation, and power analysis retain their mathematical substance. Class-set and cardinality notation are clarified, but no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim superior human-difficulty prediction, category-specific percept enhancement, and improved learning across the same three domains, retaining the 33–72% accuracy-margin gains and 20–23% training-time reductions. v2 emphasizes unmodified held-out testing, already documented in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the checkpoint results as suggesting that classification accuracy matters less than robustness for difficulty prediction, while acknowledging that early-checkpoint enhancements were not tested with humans. It also connects central perturbation concentration to changes around image subjects. Existing clinical-bias, homogenization, and hallucination limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix S1 adds task-specific fine-tuning learning rates, batch sizes, attack-step settings, and heat-map construction details. The reproducibility statement changes from promising future code release to stating that code is provided, although both PDFs already contain the same repository link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lake et al. on one-shot learning and Bomatter et al. and Gupta et al. on contextual reasoning and visual search. These modestly broaden the background without changing the central positioning against machine-teaching and image-enhancement work. Gaziv's citation-year update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodological overview, and substantial results/discussion passages are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized to introduce the component methods before the retained learning procedure in new Section 3.4. Terminology, title wording, institutional information, and numerous explanations are refined.

P2.justification: v2 adds the spatial heat map, trial-inclusion comparison, and checkpoint composite in Figs. S2, S5, and S8. Existing figures receive axis, legend, color, and caption refinements, while appendix figures and tables are relocated and renumbered. The main visual organization and table structures remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The added trial-inclusion and checkpoint checks strengthen support for existing findings, while fine-tuning disclosures and rewritten explanations improve reproducibility and clarity. The principal human-learning evidence remains unchanged. The unexplained reversal of the moth enhancement significance result limits confidence in that particular revision, but the documented gains support a modest overall improvement.
